title: Paya Soup

seo.title: Paya Soup Recipe: Authentic Pakistani Mutton Trotter Soup
seo.metaDescription: Master authentic Pakistani Paya Soup with our easy recipe. Learn how to make this rich, flavorful mutton trotter soup at home. Perfect for a hearty meal!
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageAlt: A steaming bowl of authentic Pakistani Paya Soup garnished with fresh ginger, cilantro, and green chilies.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy a comforting bowl of homemade Paya Soup, a traditional Pakistani delicacy perfect for chilly evenings.

description: Paya Soup is a rich and gelatinous Pakistani delicacy made from slow-cooked trotters, renowned for its hearty and deeply flavorful broth. This traditional soup is simmered with aromatic spices, creating a comforting and nourishing meal perfect for chilly weather or special occasions. Its unique texture and robust taste make it a beloved staple in Pakistani cuisine.

ingredients.notes: cinnamon stick, green cardamom, cloves, bay leaf

instructions.title: Clean and Prepare Paya
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the mutton trotters by washing them multiple times under cold water. You may need to scrape them or blanch them for a few minutes to remove any impurities and strong odor. Drain well and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat cooking oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown. Add the ginger-garlic paste and whole spices, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Brown the Paya and Add Spices
instructions.text: Add the cleaned mutton trotters to the pot. Sear them for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned. Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly to coat the paya with spices.

instructions.title: Add Yogurt and Water
instructions.text: Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt, mixing it in quickly to prevent curdling. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the oil separates. Pour in 6-8 cups of water, ensuring the paya are fully submerged.

instructions.title: Pressure Cook Until Tender
instructions.text: Cover the pot and if using a pressure cooker, cook on high pressure for 35-40 minutes (or according to your cooker's instructions) after it reaches full pressure. If using a regular pot, simmer on low heat for 3-4 hours, or until the paya are extremely tender and the meat easily falls off the bone. Release pressure naturally or manually.

instructions.title: Final Simmer and Garnish
instructions.text: Once the paya are tender, open the pot. Stir in the garam masala powder and let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the soup to thicken slightly. Adjust salt if needed. Garnish generously with julienned fresh ginger, sliced green chilies, and fresh cilantro before serving.

tips: Thorough cleaning of paya is crucial to remove any impurities and strong odor; blanching for 5 minutes can help achieve this.
For an even richer and more authentic flavor, consider browning the onions to a deep golden color, almost caramelized, before adding other ingredients.
Paya Soup tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Reheat gently and adjust consistency with a little water if needed.
